title: The status file names no commit a sibling can pin
foundBy: user report (host): "Could we do this instead with the JSON status files that are published by the builds for dashboard consumption?"
details: `make repin` in each project pins its codesweep-ai tools at main's tip, which may be a commit CI failed, is still building, or never built. The status file lists runs with seven-character SHAs, and finding the newest passing push build in it takes a parser. A top-level `built` field holding the full SHA lets a Makefile read it with one `sed`, from Pages rather than the rate-limited API.

notes.text: A project that publishes images has its commit named as `built` only once its `publish images` run for that commit has passed as well. Something that pins the commit may install its image, and before then there is none.

`built` is now an object: the commit, and the versions it was published under. Those are its Go module version, its image tags and its npm versions, and every run records the same for its own commit. An npm pin needs the version rather than the SHA, and the history shows what each build published.

`built` is now a list of up to 10 builds, newest first, so a repin waiting for a commit it pushed still finds it after a newer build. It reads `ci`'s own runs, and a project that publishes images needs the `publish images` commit status on the commit (DSH-019). `make repin` keeps a pin whose project lists no build, rather than moving it to the tip.

The image check reads the registry, not the commit status, and the action's own job makes one GitHub API call: the run history. Its workflows, go.mod and details come from the checkout and the event, and git says whether a build is still on the branch.
